12.name: rosa explains the codicil
12.description: Rosa tells Daniel that the codicil was not a punishment but a deliberate recognition of the family's situation and his separate life.
evidence: "I will say it again," Rosa said, "because I want you to hear it the second time. She saw through it. And it did not matter. She loved you, Daniel. She loved you the way she loved you, which was not the way you wanted to be loved, and she knew it was not the way you wanted to be loved, and she could not change the way she loved you any more than you could change the way you wanted to be loved, and she made her peace with that long before she got sick. The codicil was not a punishment. It was not even a correction. It was, as far as I could tell from the conversations I had with her in the kitchen on the afternoons when she was telling me what she was thinking — and she did tell me, Daniel, she told me because there was no one else in the house to tell — it was a recognition. She recognized that the house had become a place she lived in with me and that Lucia visited often, and she recognized that you had built a life elsewhere, and she recognized that leaving the house to you would force you to either sell it, which would cost you something, or keep it, which would cost you more, and she decided that what she wanted to leave you was the freedom from that decision. She thought she was being kind to you."
